anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, R4 (19k6) is connected between the 5 V output node (right of L1, the same node as the top of R5) and the REG_FB node (bottom of R5 / top of R6). It therefore sits in parallel with the upper feedback resistor R5 (6k8). The schematic's own note states 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)' and the spec defines this rail as 5 V.
anomalies.expected: The feedback divider should be R5 (top) and R6 (bottom) only, giving Vout = 0.8*(1+6800/1300) ≈ 4.98 V ≈ 5 V, as stated in the schematic note and in the spec ('MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V', '9A @ 5V max'). Any feedforward element across the top of the divider must be a capacitor (no DC path); a 19k6 DC-conducting resistor there is not part of the intended divider.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: R5 6k8, R6 1k3, R4 19k6; note 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)'
A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V ... feedback divider relation 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)' ... '9A @ 5V max.'

anomalies.impact: R4 in parallel with R5 reduces the effective top resistance to 6.8k||19.6k ≈ 4.8 kΩ, so Vout = 0.8*(1+4800/1300) ≈ 3.7 V instead of 5 V. The 5 V rail (servo/PWM bank, GPS module, CH330 USB-UART bridges) would be undervolted and the board would not behave as intended.

parsed.summary: The board matches the spec almost everywhere (correct MCUs, sensors, addresses, R1=10mΩ shunt, L1=15µH, 3.3 V LDO, and the documented barometer RESET/EOC pin swap is a known bug, not an anomaly). The one deviation supported by the drawing is R4 (19k6) placed across the top of the buck's feedback divider, which contradicts the schematic's own 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)' note and the spec's 5 V rail, pulling the 5 V output down to roughly 3.7 V.
